questions.title: Surgeons and Doctors
questions.stem: All surgeons are doctors. Some doctors work in hospitals. No surgeons are untrained.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some surgeons work in hospitals.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some doctors work in hospitals, but those doctors may not include any surgeons. The premises do not establish which doctors work in hospitals.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No untrained people are surgeons.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No surgeons are untrained. By the symmetry of universal negative statements, no untrained people are surgeons.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All doctors are surgeons.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All surgeons are doctors — not the reverse. Many doctors are not surgeons (e.g. GPs, psychiatrists). This reverses the universal statement.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All surgeons are trained.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 'No surgeons are untrained' is equivalent to saying every surgeon is trained. This follows directly.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some people who work in hospitals are doctors.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some doctors work in hospitals. Those hospital-working doctors are, by definition, both hospital workers and doctors.

questions.title: Charity Donations by Region
questions.stem: A charity recorded the total donations (in thousands of pounds) received from four UK regions over three months.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Donations from every region increased from November to December.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: SE: 38→65 (up). NW: 31→50 (up). Scotland: 20→35 (up). Wales: 12→22 (up). All increased.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: South East donated more than all other regions combined in October.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: SE October = 42. Others combined = 28 + 15 + 10 = 53. 42 < 53.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Scotland's donations more than doubled from October to December.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Scotland October = 15, December = 35. Double of 15 = 30. 35 > 30, so yes it more than doubled.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: South East donations decreased between October and November.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: SE October = 42, November = 38. The donations fell by £4,000.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Wales contributed more than 15% of total donations in December.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: December total = 65 + 50 + 35 + 22 = 172. Wales = 22. 22/172 ≈ 12.8%. 12.8% is less than 15%, so Wales did not contribute more than 15%.

questions.title: Mandatory Organ Donation
questions.stem: All citizens should be automatically registered as organ donors unless they choose to opt out.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes; countries with opt-out systems have significantly higher organ donation rates, which directly reduces the number of patients dying while waiting for transplants.

options.label: B
options.text: No; the government should not make decisions about people's bodies without their explicit written consent.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes; most people intend to donate their organs but simply never get around to registering.

options.label: D
options.text: No; organ transplants are expensive and place a burden on the NHS budget.

questions.answer_reason: Option A is the strongest argument because it provides concrete, evidence-based reasoning — opt-out systems demonstrably save lives by increasing available organs. Option B raises a valid ethical concern but does not address the life-saving benefit. Option C is speculative about people's intentions. Option D is irrelevant to the opt-out registration question and makes a weak cost argument.

questions.title: Hotel Room Allocation
questions.stem:
Four guests – Priya, Quinn, Ravi, and Suki – are each assigned a different room on floors 1 to 4 of a hotel.

• Ravi is on a higher floor than Priya.
• Suki is on floor 3.
• Quinn is not on a floor adjacent to Suki's floor.

Which floor is Ravi on?
questions.answer_reason: Suki is on floor 3. Quinn cannot be adjacent to Suki (not floor 2 or 4), so Quinn = floor 1. Remaining floors for Priya and Ravi: 2 and 4. Ravi is higher than Priya, so Priya = 2, Ravi = 4.

questions.title: Gym Membership Types
questions.stem:
A gym has 30 members. 10 have pool access only, 8 have gym-floor access only, and 12 have both pool and gym-floor access.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
questions.answer_reason: Pool only = 10 (set1_only). Both = 12 (set1_set2). Gym floor only = 8 (set2_only). Total = 10 + 12 + 8 = 30. Only option A has all three values correct. B swaps set1_only and set2_only. C puts the overlap as 10 and pool-only as 12. D puts the overlap as 8.

questions.title: Vaccines and Immunisation
questions.stem: All approved vaccines undergo clinical trials. Some clinical trials are funded by the government. No approved vaccines are untested.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some approved vaccines are funded by the government.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some clinical trials are government-funded, but we cannot determine whether the trials for approved vaccines specifically are among those. The overlap is not established.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All approved vaccines have been tested.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 'No approved vaccines are untested' is logically equivalent to 'all approved vaccines have been tested.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All things that undergo clinical trials are approved vaccines.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All approved vaccines undergo trials, but many drugs undergo trials and are never approved. This reverses the premise.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some government-funded trials involve approved vaccines.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: We know some trials are government-funded and all approved vaccines undergo trials, but the government-funded trials could all be for non-vaccine products. The connection is not established.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: No untested products are approved vaccines.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: No approved vaccines are untested. By symmetry of the universal negative, no untested products are approved vaccines.

questions.title: Train Delays
questions.stem: A commuter rail service runs 200 trains per week. Records show that 30 trains are delayed each week. Of the delayed trains, 80% arrive within 10 minutes of the scheduled time. Of the trains that are on time, 5% are recorded as delayed due to a logging error.

options.label: A
options.text: The probability that a randomly selected train is genuinely delayed by more than 10 minutes is 3%.

options.label: B
options.text: More than 40 trains per week are logged as delayed.

options.label: C
options.text: If a train is logged as delayed, there is approximately a 50% chance it is genuinely delayed.

options.label: D
options.text: More than 15 on-time trains per week are incorrectly logged as delayed.

questions.answer_reason: 30 trains are delayed. 20% of those (6 trains) are delayed by more than 10 min. 6/200 = 3%, so A is correct. On-time = 170. Logging errors: 170 × 0.05 = 8.5. Total logged delayed: 30 + 8.5 = 38.5, not > 40, so B is wrong. P(genuine | logged) = 30/38.5 ≈ 78%, not 50%, so C is wrong. Only 8.5 on-time trains are falsely logged, not >15, so D is wrong.

questions.title: Science Fair Entries
questions.stem:
The diagram shows students categorised by which science subjects they entered projects in at the school fair. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents students who entered projects in both Physics and Chemistry but not Biology?
questions.answer_reason: Physics = parallelogram (set1), Chemistry = star (set2), Biology = oval (set3). The region inside Physics AND Chemistry but outside Biology is set1_set2 = M. N is Physics ∩ Biology (no Chemistry). P is Chemistry ∩ Biology (no Physics). Q is all three. Answer: B (Letter M).

questions.title: The Rise of Telemedicine
questions.stem: The adoption of telemedicine accelerated dramatically during the pandemic, with virtual consultations rising by over 300% in the UK. Many patients reported shorter waiting times and greater convenience, particularly those in rural areas who previously faced long journeys to clinics. However, critics noted that physical examinations remained impossible through video calls, and elderly patients often struggled with the required technology. The British Medical Association recommended a hybrid model, where routine follow-ups and minor ailments could be handled remotely, but initial assessments and complex conditions should remain face-to-face.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Virtual consultations became more common during the pandemic.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states that virtual consultations rose by over 300% during the pandemic, which directly supports this conclusion.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All elderly patients were unable to access telemedicine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says elderly patients 'often struggled' with the technology — 'often' does not mean 'all'. Some elderly patients may have managed successfully.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The BMA recommended that all medical consultations should be conducted remotely.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The BMA recommended a hybrid model — remote for routine follow-ups and minor ailments, but face-to-face for initial assessments and complex conditions. Not all consultations remotely.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Patients in rural areas particularly benefited from telemedicine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states rural patients previously faced long journeys and that they reported shorter waiting times and greater convenience through telemedicine.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Physical examinations can be conducted effectively through video calls.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage explicitly states that physical examinations 'remained impossible through video calls.'

questions.title: Hospital Bed Occupancy
questions.stem: A hospital trust recorded the percentage bed occupancy rate across four wards over three quarters.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: A&E had the highest occupancy rate in every quarter.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: In Q2: A&E = 88%, Surgical = 90%. Surgical was higher in Q2.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Paediatric ward had the lowest occupancy in every quarter.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Q1: 70% (lowest). Q2: 65% (lowest). Q3: 72% (lowest). Paediatric is consistently the lowest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Maternity occupancy increased from Q1 to Q3.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Maternity Q1 = 78%, Q3 = 80%. 80 > 78, so it increased overall (though it dipped in Q3 from Q2's 82%).

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The range of occupancy across all wards was smallest in Q2.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Q1 range: 92 - 70 = 22. Q2 range: 90 - 65 = 25. Q3 range: 95 - 72 = 23. Q2 has the largest range, not the smallest.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Surgical ward occupancy peaked in Q2.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Surgical: Q1 = 85, Q2 = 90, Q3 = 88. The highest value is 90 in Q2.

questions.title: Swimming Relay Order
questions.stem:
A swimming team of four – Anna, Ben, Clara, and Dev – must swim a relay in a set order (1st to 4th).

• Clara swims immediately before Dev.
• Anna swims 4th.
• Ben swims before Clara.

Who swims 1st?
questions.answer_reason: Anna = 4th. Clara is immediately before Dev, forming (C, D). Ben swims before Clara. If C=2nd, D=3rd: Ben must be before Clara, so Ben=1st. Order: Ben, Clara, Dev, Anna. If C=1st, D=2nd: Ben must be before Clara(1st) — impossible. If C=3rd, D=4th: but Anna is 4th — conflict. Only valid solution: Ben(1st), Clara(2nd), Dev(3rd), Anna(4th). Ben swims 1st.

questions.title: Single-Use Plastic Ban
questions.stem: All single-use plastics should be banned immediately.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes; plastic pollution in oceans is responsible for the deaths of over one million marine animals each year, and a ban would directly reduce this harm.

options.label: B
options.text: No; an immediate ban would cause significant disruption to the food packaging industry, leading to job losses and higher food prices.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes; many countries have already banned single-use plastics, so the UK should do the same.

options.label: D
options.text: No; people can simply recycle plastics instead of banning them.

questions.answer_reason: Option B is the strongest argument because it directly addresses the 'immediately' aspect of the proposal with concrete, serious economic consequences — industry disruption, job losses, and food price increases. Option A provides a compelling environmental reason but does not address the 'immediately' qualifier. Option C is a weak appeal to other countries' actions. Option D oversimplifies — recycling rates for plastics remain very low.

questions.title: Tea and Coffee Drinkers
questions.stem:
The diagram shows beverage preferences among office workers. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents workers who drink tea but neither coffee nor hot chocolate?
questions.answer_reason: Tea = isosceles triangle (set1), Coffee = oval (set2), Hot Chocolate = star (set3). Region A (set1_only) is inside Tea but outside Coffee and Hot Chocolate. B is Tea ∩ Coffee. C is Coffee only. D is Coffee ∩ Hot Chocolate. Answer: A.

questions.title: Medical Test Accuracy
questions.stem: A hospital uses a blood test to detect a rare condition. The test has a sensitivity of 98% and a specificity of 92%. In the tested population of 5,000 patients, 50 actually have the condition.

options.label: A
options.text: The test will correctly identify all 50 patients with the condition.

options.label: B
options.text: A patient who tests positive has a greater than 50% chance of having the condition.

options.label: C
options.text: Approximately 445 patients will test positive in total.

options.label: D
options.text: The test will produce fewer than 300 false positive results.

questions.answer_reason: True positives: 50 × 0.98 = 49. False positives: 4,950 × 0.08 = 396. Total positives: 49 + 396 = 445, so C is correct. A is wrong — sensitivity is 98%, so 1 patient will be missed. PPV = 49/445 ≈ 11%, far below 50%, so B is wrong. D is wrong — 396 false positives is more than 300.

questions.title: Mammals and Whales
questions.stem: All whales are mammals. All mammals breathe air. Some mammals live on land.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All whales breathe air.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All whales are mammals and all mammals breathe air. By transitive reasoning, all whales breathe air.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some whales live on land.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some mammals live on land, but those land-dwelling mammals could all be non-whale species. The premises do not establish that any whales live on land.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All things that breathe air are mammals.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The premise states all mammals breathe air — not the reverse. Birds and reptiles also breathe air but are not mammals.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All mammals are whales.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All whales are mammals — not the reverse. Dogs, cats, and humans are mammals but not whales.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some things that breathe air are whales.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All whales breathe air (established above). Since whales exist, some air-breathing things are whales.

questions.title: A-Level Results by Subject
questions.stem: A sixth form college recorded the percentage of students achieving grades A*–B in four A-Level subjects over three years.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Chemistry showed a consistent improvement across all three years.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Chemistry: 44 → 49 → 51. Each year is higher than the previous. Consistent improvement.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: English had the highest percentage in every year.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: In 2024: English = 57%, Mathematics = 58%. Mathematics was higher in 2024.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Mathematics performance decreased from 2024 to 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Mathematics 2024 = 58%, 2025 = 55%. It decreased by 3 percentage points.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Biology improved by more than 10 percentage points from 2023 to 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Biology 2023 = 48%, 2025 = 54%. Improvement = 6 percentage points, which is not more than 10.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The average percentage across all subjects was higher in 2025 than in 2023.

questions.title: Science Lab Schedule
questions.stem:
Four experiments – P, Q, R, and S – must be completed in four consecutive lab slots (9am, 10am, 11am, 12pm).

• Experiment R is completed before experiment Q.
• Experiment S is at 11am.
• Experiment P is completed immediately before experiment R.

Which experiment is at 9am?
questions.answer_reason: P is immediately before R, forming the consecutive pair (P, R). S is at 11am. R is before Q. If P=9am, R=10am: S=11am, Q=12pm. R(10am) before Q(12pm) ✓. This works. If P=10am, R=11am: but S is at 11am — conflict. If P=11am: S is at 11am — conflict. So P must be at 9am.

questions.title: Student Societies
questions.stem:
In a university of 25 first-year students, 6 joined only the Drama society, 4 joined only the Music society, 3 joined only the Debate society, 5 joined both Drama and Music, 2 joined both Music and Debate, and 5 are not in any society.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
questions.answer_reason: Drama only = 6, Drama ∩ Music = 5, Music only = 4, Music ∩ Debate = 2, Debate only = 3, outside = 5. Total = 6+5+4+2+3+5 = 25. Only option A has all values correct. B swaps Drama-only and the Drama-Music overlap. C swaps the two overlap regions. D swaps Music-only with Debate-only and the two overlaps.

questions.title: Antibiotic Resistance
questions.stem: Antibiotic resistance has been identified by the World Health Organisation as one of the greatest threats to global health. Overuse of antibiotics in both human medicine and agriculture has accelerated the development of resistant bacteria. In hospitals, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) infections have declined in recent years due to improved hygiene protocols, but resistance to last-resort antibiotics such as carbapenems is rising. Some researchers argue that without new classes of antibiotics, routine surgical procedures could become life-threatening within decades. Pharmaceutical companies have been reluctant to invest in antibiotic research because the drugs are used for short courses, making them less profitable than treatments for chronic conditions.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Antibiotic resistance is caused solely by their use in human medicine.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states overuse occurs 'in both human medicine and agriculture' — it is not solely human medicine.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: MRSA infections in hospitals have increased in recent years.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage explicitly states MRSA infections 'have declined in recent years due to improved hygiene protocols.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Pharmaceutical companies find antibiotic development less profitable than drugs for chronic conditions.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states companies are reluctant to invest because antibiotics 'are used for short courses, making them less profitable than treatments for chronic conditions.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Resistance to all types of antibiotics has declined.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: While MRSA declined, resistance to last-resort antibiotics like carbapenems is rising. Not all resistance has declined.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Without new antibiotics, some surgical procedures may become dangerous.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states that 'without new classes of antibiotics, routine surgical procedures could become life-threatening within decades.'

questions.title: Compulsory Voting
questions.stem: Voting in general elections should be made compulsory for all eligible citizens.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes; compulsory voting ensures that elected governments reflect the views of the entire population rather than just those motivated enough to vote.

options.label: B
options.text: No; forcing people to vote undermines the principle of freedom, as the right to abstain is itself a form of political expression.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes; countries with compulsory voting tend to have more stable governments.

options.label: D
options.text: No; enforcing compulsory voting would be costly and difficult to administer.

questions.answer_reason: Option A is the strongest argument because it directly addresses the democratic legitimacy problem — governments would more accurately represent the whole population. Option B raises a philosophical concern about freedom but does not counter the democratic benefit. Option C makes a vague, unsupported claim. Option D is a weak practical objection that doesn't address the principle.

questions.title: Genetic Screening
questions.stem: A genetic screening test for a hereditary condition has an accuracy of 97% for carriers and 95% for non-carriers. In a population of 2,000 people screened, 60 are carriers of the gene.

options.label: A
options.text: More than 200 people will test positive in total.

options.label: B
options.text: A person who tests positive has approximately a 37% chance of being a carrier.

options.label: C
options.text: The test will correctly identify all 60 carriers.

options.label: D
options.text: Fewer than 50 non-carriers will receive a false positive result.

questions.answer_reason: True positives: 60 × 0.97 = 58.2. False positives: 1,940 × 0.05 = 97. Total positives: 58.2 + 97 = 155.2. PPV = 58.2/155.2 ≈ 37.5%, so B is correct. A: total positives ≈ 155, not >200, so A is wrong. C: the test misses 3% of carriers (≈ 1.8), so it will not identify all 60, so C is wrong. D: 97 false positives is not fewer than 50, so D is wrong.

questions.title: Holiday Activities
questions.stem:
The diagram shows guests at a resort categorised by activities they participated in. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents guests who went swimming and hiking but not cycling?
questions.answer_reason: Swimming = trapezoid (set1), Hiking = hexagon (set2), Cycling = parallelogram (set3). Swimming AND Hiking but NOT Cycling = set1_set2 = T. U is Swimming ∩ Cycling. V is Hiking ∩ Cycling. Z is all three. Answer: B (Letter T).

questions.title: Magazine Shelf Order
questions.stem:
Five magazines – Art, Business, Cooking, Design, and Engineering – are placed on a shelf from left (position 1) to right (position 5).

• Cooking is immediately to the right of Art.
• Engineering is in position 5.
• Business is not next to Cooking.
• Design is to the left of Business.
• Art is not in position 1.

What is in position 1?
questions.answer_reason: Engineering = position 5. (Art, Cooking) is a consecutive pair. Art ≠ position 1. If A=2, C=3: Business not next to C(3) → Business ≠ 2 or 4. Business ≠ 2 (Art). So Business ≠ 4 either. Only remaining spot is 1. Design left of Business(1) — impossible. If A=3, C=4: Business ≠ 3 or 5 (not next to C at 4, and 5 is taken). So Business = 1 or 2. Design left of Business: if B=2, D=1; if B=1, no room for D to the left. So D=1, B=2, A=3, C=4, E=5. Check: Business(2) next to Cooking(4)? No ✓. Position 1 = Design.

questions.title: Energy Consumption by Source
questions.stem: A report tracked the percentage of energy generated from different sources in a country over three years.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Renewable sources (wind and solar combined) exceeded 40% of energy generation in 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Wind 2025 = 30%, Solar 2025 = 15%. Combined = 45%, which exceeds 40%.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Gas remained the single largest source of energy in every year.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: 2023: Gas 45% (highest). 2024: Gas 40% (highest). 2025: Gas 35% — Wind is 30%, so Gas is still highest at 35%.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Nuclear energy increased as a proportion over the three years.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Nuclear: 20% → 18% → 17%. It decreased each year.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Solar energy's share tripled from 2023 to 2025.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Solar 2023 = 8%, 2025 = 15%. Triple of 8% = 24%. 15% is less than 24%, so it did not triple.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The combined share of non-renewable sources (gas, nuclear, other) fell below 60% by 2025.

questions.title: Social Media and Mental Health
questions.stem: Research published in the Journal of Adolescent Health found a correlation between heavy social media use and increased rates of anxiety and depression in teenagers. The study followed 3,000 participants aged 13–18 over two years. Those who spent more than three hours daily on social media were twice as likely to report poor mental health outcomes. However, the researchers cautioned that correlation does not imply causation — teenagers already experiencing mental health difficulties may turn to social media for connection. Several schools have introduced phone-free policies during lesson hours, reporting improved concentration but no measurable change in students' overall wellbeing scores.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The study proved that social media causes anxiety and depression in teenagers.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage found a correlation, not causation. The researchers explicitly cautioned that 'correlation does not imply causation.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Teenagers who used social media heavily were more likely to report poor mental health.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states those spending more than three hours daily were 'twice as likely to report poor mental health outcomes.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Phone-free policies in schools improved students' overall wellbeing.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Schools reported 'improved concentration but no measurable change in students' overall wellbeing scores.' Wellbeing did not improve.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: The study participants were all adults.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The study followed participants 'aged 13–18' — these are teenagers, not adults.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: It is possible that teenagers with existing mental health problems use social media more.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states researchers cautioned that 'teenagers already experiencing mental health difficulties may turn to social media for connection,' which supports this possibility.

questions.title: Instrument Players
questions.stem:
In a music school of 18 students, 5 play piano only, 4 play guitar only, 3 play violin only, 2 play both piano and guitar, and 4 play both guitar and violin.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
questions.answer_reason: Piano only = 5, Piano ∩ Guitar = 2, Guitar only = 4, Guitar ∩ Violin = 4, Violin only = 3. Total = 5+2+4+4+3 = 18. Only option B has all values correct. A swaps the two overlaps. C swaps piano-only and guitar-only. D swaps piano-only and violin-only.

questions.title: Abolishing Private Schools
questions.stem: Private schools should be abolished and all children should attend state schools.

options.label: A
options.text: Yes; private schools entrench social inequality by giving wealthier children access to better resources, creating an uneven playing field from childhood.

options.label: B
options.text: No; parents have the right to choose how to spend their money, including on their children's education.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes; removing private schools would force the government to invest more in state education.

options.label: D
options.text: No; many private schools have historic buildings and traditions that would be lost.

questions.answer_reason: Option A is the strongest argument because it identifies a specific, measurable harm — entrenched social inequality from childhood — that directly supports the proposal. Option B raises parental rights but doesn't address the inequality concern. Option C is speculative about what the government might do. Option D is irrelevant — buildings and traditions do not justify educational inequality.

questions.title: Bus Arrival Order
questions.stem:
Four buses – Route 7, Route 12, Route 15, and Route 22 – arrive at a station one after another.

• Route 15 arrives immediately after Route 7.
• Route 22 does not arrive 1st or 4th.
• Route 12 arrives after Route 22.

Which bus arrives 4th?
questions.answer_reason: Route 15 is immediately after Route 7, so (7, 15) is consecutive. Route 22 is not 1st or 4th. Route 12 is after Route 22. If 7=1st, 15=2nd: Route 22 not 1st (taken) or 4th, so 22=3rd. Route 12 after 22(3rd), so 12=4th ✓. If 7=2nd, 15=3rd: 22 not 1st or 4th, so 22 must be a remaining slot. Remaining: 1st and 4th for 22 and 12. But 22 ≠ 1st or 4th — no valid placement. If 7=3rd, 15=4th: 22 ≠ 1st or 4th. Remaining: 1st and 2nd for 22 and 12. 12 after 22 → 22=1st, but 22 ≠ 1st — contradiction. Only valid solution: 7,15,22,12. Route 12 arrives 4th.

questions.title: Allergy Types
questions.stem:
A survey of 40 patients found: 12 are allergic to peanuts only, 8 are allergic to shellfish only, 6 are allergic to both peanuts and shellfish, and 14 are allergic to neither.

Which of the following diagrams best represents the data?
questions.answer_reason: Peanuts only = 12, both = 6, shellfish only = 8, neither = 14. Total = 12+6+8+14 = 40 ✓. Only option A is correct. B swaps peanuts and shellfish counts. C puts 8 in the overlap. D swaps peanuts-only with neither.

questions.title: Renewable Energy Subsidies
questions.stem: Government subsidies for renewable energy projects have increased steadily over the past decade. Wind farm installations have tripled in number since 2015, while solar panel costs have fallen by 70%. Critics argue that subsidies distort the energy market and discourage private investment by making companies dependent on government support. Proponents counter that subsidies are essential during the early stages of technology adoption and can be phased out once renewables achieve cost parity with fossil fuels. In 2024, several offshore wind projects were completed ahead of schedule and under budget, suggesting the industry is maturing. However, onshore wind planning applications continue to face significant local opposition in many rural areas.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Government subsidies for renewable energy have decreased over the past decade.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states subsidies 'have increased steadily over the past decade,' not decreased.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Solar panel costs have fallen significantly.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states solar panel costs 'have fallen by 70%,' which is a significant reduction.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All wind projects are completed on time and under budget.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage says 'several offshore wind projects' were completed ahead of schedule — 'several' does not mean all, and it only refers to offshore projects.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Critics believe subsidies can create dependency in energy companies.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage states critics argue subsidies 'discourage private investment by making companies dependent on government support.'

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Onshore wind projects face no opposition.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: The passage explicitly states 'onshore wind planning applications continue to face significant local opposition in many rural areas.'

questions.title: GP Surgery Appointments
questions.stem: A GP surgery recorded the number of appointments booked per week across four categories.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Face-to-face appointments were the most common type every week.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Week 1: 120 (highest). Week 2: 115 (highest). Week 3: 130 (highest). Week 4: 125 (highest). Face-to-face leads every week.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Video appointments increased every week.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Video: 15, 20, 18, 25. It decreased from Week 2 (20) to Week 3 (18).

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Total appointments in Week 4 exceeded 250.
Home visits were fewer than video appointments in every week.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: W1: 10 < 15. W2: 8 < 20. W3: 12 < 18. W4: 9 < 25. Home visits are always fewer.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Telephone appointments decreased from Week 1 to Week 2.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Telephone Week 1 = 85, Week 2 = 90. It increased, not decreased.

questions.title: Campus Facilities
questions.stem:
The diagram shows students categorised by which campus facilities they use. Each letter marks a different region.

Which letter represents students who use the Library only?
questions.answer_reason: Library = hexagon (set1), Canteen = trapezoid (set2), Sports Hall = isosceles triangle (set3). Region H (set1_only) is inside the hexagon but outside the trapezoid and triangle — Library only. J is Library ∩ Canteen. K is Canteen only. M is outside all. Answer: C (Letter H).

questions.title: Card Drawing Probability
questions.stem: A bag contains 8 red cards, 5 blue cards, and 7 green cards. Two cards are drawn at random without replacement.

options.label: A
options.text: The probability that both cards are red is approximately 15%.

options.label: B
options.text: The probability that both cards are the same colour is greater than 40%.

options.label: C
options.text: The probability of drawing one red and one blue card (in any order) is approximately 10%.

options.label: D
options.text: The probability that at least one card is green is less than 50%.

questions.answer_reason: Total cards = 20. P(both red) = (8/20)(7/19) = 56/380 ≈ 14.7% ≈ 15%, so A is correct. P(same colour) = 56/380 + 20/380 + 42/380 = 118/380 ≈ 31%, not >40%, so B is wrong. P(one red, one blue) = 2 × (8/20)(5/19) = 80/380 ≈ 21%, not ≈10%, so C is wrong. P(≥1 green) ≈ 59%, not <50%, so D is wrong.

questions.title: Nurses and Healthcare Workers
questions.stem: All nurses are healthcare workers. All healthcare workers must be registered. Some healthcare workers specialise in mental health.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All nurses must be registered.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All nurses are healthcare workers, and all healthcare workers must be registered. By transitive reasoning, all nurses must be registered.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some nurses specialise in mental health.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: Some healthcare workers specialise in mental health, but those may not include any nurses. The premises do not establish which healthcare workers specialise in mental health.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All healthcare workers are nurses.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All nurses are healthcare workers — not the reverse. Doctors, paramedics, and therapists are healthcare workers but not nurses.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some registered people are healthcare workers.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All healthcare workers must be registered. Since healthcare workers exist, some registered people must be healthcare workers.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: All people who must be registered are healthcare workers.
decision_making_question_statements.answer_reason: All healthcare workers must be registered, but other professionals (e.g. lawyers, accountants) may also need registration. The reverse does not hold.

questions.title: Student Transport Survey
questions.stem:
The diagram shows how students travel to school. Each letter marks a region.

Which letter represents students who walk to school but do not cycle?
questions.answer_reason: Walk = parallelogram (set1), Cycle = star (set2). Region E (set1_only) is inside the parallelogram but outside the star — students who walk but do not cycle. F is Walk ∩ Cycle. G is Cycle only. H is outside both (neither walk nor cycle). Answer: C (Letter E).
